Parents choose private over government schools despite similar outcomes

Parents are increasingly opting for private schools over government institutions, even when learning outcomes are comparable. This trend is observed in various regions, including Gaza, where private schools have become a costly choice for struggling parents. The decision to choose private education often stems from factors beyond academic performance, such as perceived quality of infrastructure, teaching methods, or social environment. Despite the financial strain, the preference for private schooling persists, highlighting a complex interplay of parental aspirations, educational system perceptions, and economic realities.
